title: My first game: A cozy adventure game about running a miniature-painting shop (1 prompt)
author: glorious_sir
selftext:
I've always wanted to test this crossover and with AI it was finally possible for me to develop something like this on my own. 

Every minigame comes from the real hobby: you flood base coats with a hold-and-release brush, wash and highlight your figures on the beat, and mix rare pigments on a 2048-style tray to discover new unique colors and sell it to customers.  
  
Over the past months I've been developing my own 'Gamestudio' setup with AI. As I believe in scalability, the goal of the studio is to work as autonomous as possible with the goal of achieving good 1 day - 1 prompt results. The setup seems to finally be working. Claude developed everything end-to-end with a single prompt after about a day of non-stop coding on Opus 5.5 ultra code.

A full run takes about 45 minutes, works on desktop and phones. I built it with Claude as an AI game studio, and I'd love to hear what you think:

[https://ifr13nd.itch.io/toms-tiny-armies](https://ifr13nd.itch.io/toms-tiny-armies)

comments.author: OWazabi
comments.body:
It looks super nice, the ambiance is great!

What did you used to do all the pixel art and animations for it?

replies.author: glorious_sir
replies.body:
Hey! Thank you! I encourge to play it until the end. It's totally crazy how claude developed the whole game end-to-end. To be fair I've spend quite a bit of time setting up my game studio that is basically operating like a real game studio with agentic loops for different functions.

I believe QAing and initial sketching is the key here.

As an example: The gamestudio decided to build a bot that tests after every major milestone if the loop is still around the 45minute mark, checks for any bugs, and if the economy is balanced and so on.

Likewise the artist decided together with the engineer that for a pixel game html makes most sense and then sketched the engine.

  
The prompt:  
Develop a 30-45 minute pixel adventure game about a store owner of warhammer figures (Tom). Milestones are involved. There are minigames where he needs to invest money and get a return. Example: coloring figures with ultra rare colors that can be aquired through xyz (mixing same colors into new patterns?) just an idea. it should be a super cozy game setting genre with permanent upgrades involved throughout the journey.

That was it, depleting 5x 5h windows on 5x plan the game was published on github.
